findings.title: Runtime invariant enforced with a module-level `assert`
findings.description: The check that `_BUCKET_ROWS` covers every `TickSessionStatus` uses `assert`. Python strips asserts under `-O`, so a bucket added to the enum later would go unreported in optimized runs without any error. The project says to fail explicitly. Replace it with an explicit `if ... raise RuntimeError(...)`, or add a unit test that compares the two sets.

findings.title: Exception-to-exit-code mapping depends on a caller-supplied tuple
findings.description: `run_mapped` checks `isinstance(exc, storage)` before `exit_code_for`. This lets `TickDatabaseUnreachable` override the "preflight" mapping for the read verbs only. It works, and `tick_exit.py` already maps `TickCalendarError` and `psycopg.OperationalError` to storage. However, exit-code policy is now split between `tick_exit.py`, which the design says defines it once, and a per-verb parameter. `_read_storage()` also needs a function-local import just to build a one-element tuple. A cleaner option is a dedicated `TickReadUnreachable` exception, or a `read_only` flag passed to `exit_code_for`. As written, the "one place" invariant is weakened.

findings.title: Long functions and mixed responsibilities in the status builder and renderer
findings.description: `_product_status` is about 45 lines. It builds the wanted range, verdicts, contract lines, buckets and the DTO in one body. `_product_lines` in `tick_status_render.py` is about 60 lines, over the ~50-line guideline. `tick_status_build.py` is also about 245 lines and defines a generic `jsonable` helper. `tick_coverage.py` imports `jsonable` and other shared helpers from this module, so those helpers belong in a smaller shared module. This isn't blocking.

findings.title: `raw_counts` full-range scan
findings.description: The scan is bounded by the range's first open and last close, and the one-scan design is documented. The join to `unnest` uses `BETWEEN` on both bounds, so a trade at exactly a session boundary shared by two adjacent sessions would be counted in both. That is unlikely on real calendars, but I didn't verify it. The mismatch test only covers the midnight-crossing case.

findings.title: Positive observations
findings.description: The SQL is parameterized throughout. The tests use throwaway databases and don't read the production URL variable, and they delete by primary key rather than `ctid`. The `utc_midnight` and `days_touched` extraction removes duplicated logic from `ingest_plan.py` and `session_days.py`. The new `status` and `coverage` verbs have unit, integration and CLI coverage, including exit codes 1, 3 and 4.
